name: Foundation Fellowship
sponsor: University of Georgia (Jere W. Morehead Honors College)
summary: UGA's top academic scholarship for high school seniors with very strong records. Fellows get a yearly stipend on top of HOPE/Zell Miller, plus funded travel-study trips, an Oxford summer program, and research grants.
how_to_apply: Submit UGA's first-year admission application, then complete the Morehead Honors College/Foundation Fellowship application from your application status page by November 1. Finalists must attend interviews in late February.
amount_text: Georgia residents: $15,750 a year stipend plus the Zell Miller Scholarship, for four years, plus funded travel-study and research grants (out-of-state students get a larger stipend and a tuition waive
deadline_text: November 1 each year (the 2026 deadline has passed; next is November 1, 2027 for the class of 2028)
other_requirements: Must not have enrolled at another college as a degree-seeking student. The Bernard Ramsey Honors Scholarship was merged into the Foundation Fellowship in 2021. Fellows must live in Myers Hall the first year and keep a 3.40 UGA GPA.

name: Dr. Henry King Stanford Scholarship
summary: A UGA merit scholarship for strong students who apply for the Foundation Fellowship and are admitted to the Morehead Honors College.
how_to_apply: Apply for the Foundation Fellowship by its November 1 deadline; Stanford Scholars are chosen from that applicant pool.
amount_text: $5,000 a year stipend (out-of-state students also get a tuition waiver), renewable for up to eight semesters
deadline_text: Same as the Foundation Fellowship application: November 1
other_requirements: Must apply for the Foundation Fellowship and be admitted to the Morehead Honors College.

name: Charter Scholarship
summary: A merit scholarship for Georgia residents entering UGA as first-year students, awarded during the admission review.
how_to_apply: No separate application: admitted students are considered automatically. Awards are usually finalized by early April.
amount_text: $2,000 a year stipend, renewable for up to eight semesters
deadline_text: No separate deadline; considered with your UGA admission application
other_requirements: Competitive even though automatic: no published GPA or test cutoff.

name: Presidential Leadership Scholarship
summary: A UGA merit scholarship for incoming first-year students with strong academics and a record of leadership in school or community activities.
how_to_apply: No separate application: admitted students are considered automatically, so describe your leadership activities fully in the admission application.
amount_text: Georgia residents: $3,000 a year stipend, renewable for up to eight semesters (out-of-state students also get a tuition waiver)
deadline_text: No separate deadline; considered with your UGA admission application
other_requirements: Requires a history of co-curricular leadership.

name: Charles McDonald Brown Scholarship
summary: A UGA merit scholarship for Georgia residents entering as first-year students who have strong academics and a history of leadership.
how_to_apply: No separate application: admitted Georgia residents are considered automatically during admission review.
amount_text: $5,000 a year stipend, renewable for up to eight semesters
deadline_text: No separate deadline; considered with your UGA admission application
other_requirements: Requires a history of co-curricular leadership.

name: One UGA Scholarship
summary: A UGA merit scholarship for incoming first-year students of any residency, awarded during admission review.
how_to_apply: No separate application: admitted students are considered automatically.
amount_text: Georgia residents: $3,000 a year stipend, renewable for up to eight semesters (out-of-state: $1,500 plus a tuition waiver)
deadline_text: No separate deadline; considered with your UGA admission application

name: Georgia Commitment Scholars Program
summary: A need-based scholarship for Georgia residents at UGA, with priority for Pell Grant-eligible students. It also includes student success programs and support.
how_to_apply: No separate application: Georgia residents who file the FAFSA are screened automatically. File by December 15 for priority consideration, since funds are limited.
amount_text: Amount varies; renewable for up to four years
deadline_text: FAFSA priority date December 15 of senior year
other_requirements: Must file the FAFSA. Pell Grant-eligible students get priority.

name: Stamps President's Scholars Program
summary: Georgia Tech's top merit scholarship, about 50 awards a year. It covers the full cost of attendance plus enrichment funds, a laptop stipend, and leadership programs.
how_to_apply: Apply to Georgia Tech by Early Action: you are considered automatically, with no separate scholarship application. Semifinalists do a virtual interview, and finalists must attend Scholars Weekend in April.
amount_text: Full tuition, fees, housing, meals, and books (including HOPE/Zell Miller for Georgia residents) for four years, plus $12,000 enrichment funds and a $1,100 laptop stipend
deadline_text: Georgia residents: Early Action 1, October 15 (passed for 2026). Non-Georgia residents: Early Action 2, early November.
other_requirements: Must apply Early Action. You compete with the primary major on your application and can't change majors until the end of your first spring. No minimum GPA or test score.

name: G. Wayne Clough Georgia Tech Promise Program
summary: Need-based aid for Georgia residents from low-income families who are admitted to Georgia Tech. It helps qualifying students attend with little or no debt.
how_to_apply: No separate application: complete Georgia Tech's financial aid process (the FAFSA and any requested documents) by January 31 before your first year.
amount_text: Amount varies by need; for up to eight semesters
deadline_text: Financial aid application by January 31 of senior year; late applications are not reviewed
other_requirements: Family income and resources under $55,500 a year. Student and both parents must be legal Georgia residents. Must graduate from an accredited Georgia high school and be eligible for HOPE or Zell Miller.

name: Emory University Scholar Programs (Woodruff Scholars)
summary: Emory's merit scholarships for top first-year applicants to Emory College or Oxford College, ranging from partial to full awards, with scholar programs and mentoring.
how_to_apply: Apply to Emory (Early Decision I, Early Decision II, or Regular Decision) and answer "Yes" to the scholar programs question. Finalists are told by late February and must attend a spring campus visit.
amount_text: Partial to full merit scholarships, renewable for up to eight semesters
deadline_text: November 1 (Early Decision I) or November 15 (Early Decision II and Regular Decision) of senior year
other_requirements: Must check "Yes" to the scholar programs question on the Emory application. About 175 to 200 finalists are chosen from about 10,000 applicants.

name: Georgia State Stamps Scholarship
summary: A full scholarship for Georgia residents entering Georgia State's Honors College. It covers tuition (with HOPE/Zell), fees, housing, meals, a yearly stipend, and enrichment funds.
how_to_apply: Apply to Georgia State by the November 15 priority deadline, then submit the Stamps/Presidential scholarship application and one recommendation letter. Finalists interview in March.
amount_text: Tuition, fees, housing, and a meal plan for up to four years, plus a yearly stipend and a one-time $10,000 enrichment fund
deadline_text: November 15 of senior year (11:59 p.m. Eastern)
other_requirements: Must be an incoming in-state first-year student who qualifies for the Honors College. Sources differ on the stipend: Stamps lists $2,000 a year and Georgia State's viewbook lists $4,000 a year.

name: Georgia State Presidential Scholarship
summary: Georgia State's top merit scholarship for exceptional incoming first-year students, worth up to $28,000 a year depending on residency.
how_to_apply: Apply to Georgia State by the priority deadline, then submit the combined Stamps/Presidential scholarship application.
amount_text: Up to $28,000 a year for four years, depending on in-state or out-of-state status
deadline_text: Mid-November of senior year (Georgia State lists November 15; confirm on the scholarship portal)

name: Coca-Cola First Generation Scholarship (Georgia State)
summary: A scholarship for incoming Georgia State first-year students who will be the first in their family to go to college.
how_to_apply: Apply to Georgia State, then submit the scholarship application by February 15.
amount_text: Up to $5,000 a year for four years
deadline_text: February 15 of senior year

name: Presidential Fellows Cohort
summary: A new KSU honors scholarship starting with students entering in fall 2027. Ten Georgia students get $10,000 a year plus mentoring, a leadership curriculum, and study abroad in Italy.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a resume, short-answer responses, and contacts for two recommenders by December 15. Interviews are in February.
amount_text: $10,000 a year for up to four years, plus study abroad in Italy
deadline_text: December 15 of senior year (December 15, 2026 for fall 2027 entry)
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia resident eligible for the Zell Miller Scholarship, enter KSU as a traditional first-year student, and complete the Presidential Fellows minor. An equivalent ACT score is accepted (exact ACT score not stated).

name: First-Year Merit Scholarship
summary: A one-time automatic award for Georgia residents starting at Georgia Southern in the fall, based on the GPA calculated during admission.
how_to_apply: No separate application: apply for fall admission by February 1 and you are considered automatically. Notices go out in the spring.
amount_text: One-time award for the first year: $1,000 (4.00+ GPA), $750 (3.80-3.99), or $500 (3.50-3.79)
deadline_text: Admission application by February 1, 2027 for fall 2027 entry
other_requirements: Uses the core GPA that Georgia Southern recalculates during admission, which may differ from your school GPA. Must qualify for in-state tuition. Fall entry only; not renewable.

name: Honors College Scholarships (1906 Scholars and Honors College Scholarship)
summary: Georgia Southern's Honors College awards full-tuition (1906 Scholars) and half-tuition scholarships, plus major-specific awards, to incoming first-year students chosen through interviews.
how_to_apply: Get accepted to Georgia Southern and submit the Honors College application by January 15. Selected applicants are invited to interview at Honors Scholars' Day in February.
amount_text: Full tuition (1906 Scholars) or half tuition (Honors College Scholarship) for up to eight semesters; can be combined with HOPE/Zell
deadline_text: January 15 of senior year (priority deadline for scholarship interviews)
other_requirements: Must be admitted to the Honors College. Honors Scholars' Day interviews are February 12, 2027 (Armstrong) or February 19, 2027 (Statesboro).

name: Goel Scholars Program
summary: A full-ride scholarship for first-generation college students with financial need from Georgia or a neighboring state who enter Georgia Southern's Honors College.
how_to_apply: Follow the Honors College application steps and apply by January 15. Some applicants are invited to interview in February, and winners are told by mid-March.
amount_text: Full tuition, mandatory fees, textbooks, housing, and meal plan for up to eight semesters
deadline_text: January 15, 2027
other_requirements: Must live in Georgia, Alabama, Florida, North Carolina, South Carolina, or Tennessee. Neither parent can have a bachelor's degree. Need is based on the FAFSA.

name: Southern Leaders Scholarship
summary: A first-year award for up to 25 incoming Georgia Southern students with strong leadership and volunteer service in high school.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission, write the Honors College/leadership programs essay, and check "Yes" for interest in leadership programs by February 1. Some applicants are interviewed.
amount_text: $1,000 one-time ($500 each semester of the first year)
deadline_text: February 1 of senior year
other_requirements: GPA is calculated by the Office of Admissions.

name: President's Scholarship Competition
summary: Invited high school seniors compete on campus for Georgia College's top merit scholarships, including the Presidential Plus, Presidential, and Vera L. Vincent awards.
how_to_apply: Submit a complete Early Action admission application by October 15. Qualified students may be invited to the competition, held December 4, 2026, and must attend all of it.
amount_text: Presidential Plus $6,000 a year ($24,000 total); Presidential $4,000 a year ($16,000); Vera L. Vincent $3,000 a year ($12,000); some include study abroad stipends
deadline_text: Early Action admission deadline, October 15 of senior year (passed for 2026)
other_requirements: GPA is calculated by the Office of Admissions. Meeting the minimums does not guarantee an invitation. Gap-year students who have not enrolled in college are also eligible.

name: Stamps Scholars Program (Mercer)
summary: A full scholarship for ten incoming Mercer first-year students each year, chosen for leadership, perseverance, scholarship, service, and innovation.
how_to_apply: Apply to Mercer with all documents by November 1. Eligible admitted students are invited to Presidential Scholars Weekend interviews.
amount_text: Full tuition and fees, housing and food, an iPad, and up to $16,000 in enrichment funds over four years
deadline_text: November 1 of senior year (passed for 2026)
other_requirements: By invitation after admission review; finalists submit a portfolio. Must keep a 3.5 GPA to renew.

name: Mercer Merit Scholarship
summary: An automatic merit scholarship that every admitted first-year student at Mercer is evaluated for.
how_to_apply: No separate application: you are evaluated automatically when you are admitted.
amount_text: $18,000 to $27,000 a year, renewable with a 2.0 GPA
deadline_text: No separate deadline; awarded with admission

name: Bessie Willingham Tift Scholarship
summary: A full-tuition-plus-housing scholarship at Mercer for Georgia residents, chosen by invitation and interview.
how_to_apply: Apply to Mercer by November 1; selected Georgia applicants are invited to interview.
amount_text: Full tuition with housing and food, renewable with a 3.0 GPA
deadline_text: November 1 of senior year (passed for 2026)
other_requirements: By invitation and interview.

name: Mercer REACH Scholarship
summary: An extra Mercer award for current REACH Georgia Scholars who enroll at Mercer, on top of their state REACH award.
how_to_apply: Submit Mercer's scholarship application by December 1 and the FAFSA by February 1.
amount_text: $5,000 from Mercer plus the $2,500 state REACH award, renewable with a 2.0 GPA
deadline_text: December 1 of senior year (FAFSA by February 1)
other_requirements: Must be a current REACH Georgia Scholar.

name: Marvin B. Perry Presidential Scholarship
summary: Agnes Scott's top scholarship for admitted students, covering full tuition, housing, and dining for four years at this women's college.
how_to_apply: If invited after admission, register for Virtual Admitted Scottie Day (March 6, 2027) and submit a written or video essay through the application portal by February 8, 2027.
amount_text: Full tuition, housing, and dining for up to four years (valued at $264,000)
deadline_text: Essay due by midnight, February 8, 2027
other_requirements: Admitted students are invited to compete based on their high school record. Attending Virtual Admitted Scottie Day also earns a $2,000-a-year Campus Visit Award.

name: Signature Scholars (Bonner, Gate of Opportunity, and Whitehead Scholars)
summary: Need-based work-and-service scholarship programs at Berry for students with the highest financial need, mostly Pell-eligible. Students work on campus and families pay no more than $6,000 a year toward costs.
how_to_apply: File the FAFSA and apply in the MyBerry Portal under the Scholarships tab, ranking the programs by interest. Applicants interview.
amount_text: Covers tuition, fees, housing, and food except up to $6,000 a year paid by the student and family
deadline_text: Deadline not posted; contact Berry's Gate of Opportunity office
other_requirements: Requires campus work and engagement beyond the school year. The Whitehead program is designed especially for women.

name: James Edward Oglethorpe Scholarship
summary: Oglethorpe's top full-tuition scholarship, up to four awarded each year to students with outstanding records and strong potential to contribute to campus.
how_to_apply: Apply to Oglethorpe; selected students are invited to compete at Scholarship Weekend in January or February of senior year.
amount_text: Full tuition for four years
deadline_text: By invitation; Scholarship Weekend is in January or February of senior year
other_requirements: Must be invited to and attend the competition. Runners-up receive Oglethorpe Scholars Awards.

name: J. Fred and Catherine B. Agel Leadership Scholarship
summary: A full-tuition scholarship at Oglethorpe for up to three students a year with a deep commitment to service and community leadership.
how_to_apply: Be nominated and take part in the scholarship competition at Scholarship Weekend; winners are chosen by community involvement and an alumni interview.
amount_text: Full tuition for four years
deadline_text: By nomination; Scholarship Weekend is in January or February of senior year
other_requirements: Requires a nomination.

name: Oglethorpe Scholars Awards
summary: Automatic merit awards (Lanier, University, Oxford, Presidential, and Presidential with Recognition) given to admitted Oglethorpe students based on their academic record.
how_to_apply: No extra forms or essays: you are considered automatically when admitted.
deadline_text: No separate deadline; awarded with admission (letters go out mid-winter through spring)
other_requirements: Georgia residents who qualify for HOPE also get an OU HOPE Plus supplement.

name: Flagship 50 Tuition Match
summary: Oglethorpe caps tuition at your home state's flagship public university rate (UGA for Georgia residents) for qualifying first-year students. Georgia residents can stack HOPE and the Tuition Equalization Grant on top.
how_to_apply: No separate application stated: admitted students who meet any one of the academic minimums receive it.
amount_text: Tuition matched to your home state's flagship rate for four years
deadline_text: No separate deadline; awarded with admission for fall 2027
other_requirements: Any ONE of these qualifies: a 3.8 GPA (as calculated by Oglethorpe), a 1400 SAT superscore, or a 30 ACT superscore. Must live on campus for three years. Can't be combined with Oglethorpe's full-tuition scholarships.

name: Spelman College Merit Scholarships
summary: Admitted first-year students at Spelman, a women's college, are automatically considered for merit awards ranging from half tuition to full tuition, fees, and room and board (including the Dovey Johnson Roundtree Presidential and Dean's Scholarships).
how_to_apply: No separate application: your admission application counts as your scholarship application. Some programs (Bonner, UPS, Ralph Lauren) need a separate application.
amount_text: From half tuition up to full tuition, fees, and room and board for four years
deadline_text: No separate deadline posted; apply Early Action or Early Decision for Civic Scholar programs
other_requirements: Considered with or without test scores. Selection looks at GPA, test scores if sent, service, and leadership.

name: Jonathan Smith Scholarship
summary: A Spelman merit scholarship for students from Georgia, covering tuition, fees, and room and board.
how_to_apply: No separate application: admitted students are considered automatically by the Office of Admissions.
amount_text: Tuition, fees, and room and board for four years
deadline_text: No separate deadline posted; considered with admission
other_requirements: For Georgia students.

name: Morehouse Academic Scholarship
summary: Merit scholarships that all academically qualified first-time freshmen admitted to Morehouse, a men's college, are automatically reviewed for.
how_to_apply: No separate application: admitted students are reviewed automatically. Award emails usually go out early in the new year.
amount_text: Amount varies; some awards renew for up to four years
deadline_text: No separate deadline; awarded while funds last, so apply early
other_requirements: Morehouse is a men's college.

name: Clark Atlanta University Merit-Based Scholarship
summary: First-year applicants to Clark Atlanta with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA are automatically considered for competitive merit scholarships.
how_to_apply: No separate application: apply for admission, ideally by Early Action, with transcripts in by the deadline for priority.
amount_text: Amount not stated
deadline_text: Early Action priority November 1 (passed for 2026); final deadline March 1 of senior year
other_requirements: Meeting the 3.0 minimum does not guarantee an award.

name: Steele Scholarship
sponsor: Valdosta State University (Langdale College of Business)
summary: A renewable Valdosta State scholarship for incoming business students with strong grades and SAT scores.
how_to_apply: Apply through VSU's general scholarship application in Scholarship Universe (2027-28 applications opened October 1, 2026) and file the FAFSA if you want need considered.
amount_text: Amount not stated; renewable with a 3.25 college GPA
deadline_text: Most VSU scholarship deadlines fall early in the spring semester; check Scholarship Universe
other_requirements: Requires BOTH a 1240 SAT and a 3.25 high school GPA (4.0 scale). For business majors.

name: UWG Honors College Presidential Scholarship
summary: A full scholarship for top incoming first-year students in UWG's Honors College, covering tuition, room and board, and fees.
how_to_apply: Apply to UWG and to the Honors College by January 15. Highly qualified students are invited to interview, with decisions around March 1.
amount_text: Tuition, room and board, and fees; renewable for up to three more years
deadline_text: January 15 of senior year (Honors College application)
other_requirements: Must be eligible for the Honors College. No published GPA or test minimum.

name: Honors College Presidential Scholarship (Columbus State)
summary: Columbus State's top Honors College award for entering freshmen. The Honors College also offers Tower ($2,500 a year) and University ($1,000 one-time) scholarships.
how_to_apply: Apply to the Honors College by its deadline; admitted applicants who meet the honors requirements are considered automatically.
amount_text: Up to $5,000 a year for four years, plus a one-time study abroad stipend of up to $3,200
deadline_text: Honors College application deadline (date not posted; historically late January)
other_requirements: Must be admitted to the Honors College.

name: SCAD Academic and Achievement Scholarships
sponsor: Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD)
summary: Merit scholarships for incoming SCAD students based on academic achievement or overall achievement, considered with the admission application.
how_to_apply: Apply to SCAD and send any requested materials to your admission adviser. A portfolio and achievement profile are optional but improve your chances.
amount_text: Amount not stated; renews with a 3.0 GPA
deadline_text: No separate deadline posted; considered with admission
college: Savannah College of Art and Design

name: SCAD Challenge
sponsor: Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD)
summary: A creative competition for high school juniors and seniors that awards SCAD scholarships.
how_to_apply: Enter through SCAD's Challenge page during the school year.
amount_text: Scholarship amounts not stated
deadline_text: Check SCAD's Challenge page for this year's dates
college: Savannah College of Art and Design

name: GGC Top Honors Scholarship
summary: A limited award for strong incoming first-year students who are accepted early and admitted to GGC's Honors Program.
how_to_apply: No application needed: be accepted to GGC by December 1 and admitted to the Honors Program. A committee picks recipients, with priority to early applicants.
amount_text: $1,000 a year
deadline_text: Be accepted by December 1 of senior year; fall entry only
other_requirements: Uses the high school core GPA. Limited number of awards. Must be admitted to the Honors Program.

name: Young Harris College Merit Scholarships
summary: Every new Young Harris student is considered for one of four merit scholarship tiers.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission; all new students are considered for merit awards.
amount_text: $16,000 to $20,000 a year, depending on tier
deadline_text: No separate deadline posted; considered with admission
other_requirements: Tier criteria are not published; contact the financial aid office.
